title: continuous-batching: scheduler tuning to improve queueing fairness and prevent starvation
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context: continuous-batching in the serving runtime improved throughput but we've observed latency tail regressions for low-volume customers and starvation for small, long-lived requests when high-volume prefixes dominate the batch window. This PR tunes the scheduler heuristics to balance batching efficiency with fairness and bounded latency.

Motivation: customer-facing incident SUP-447 showed that a minority of long-polling requests were never scheduled during heavy traffic patterns, causing 99th-percentile latency to spike and impacting SLAs. We need safeguards to avoid starvation while preserving the benefits of grouping similar requests.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces a per-queue aging score: requests accrue priority the longer they wait, allowing the scheduler to prefer older requests once they cross age thresholds.
- Adds a max-wait timeout that forces a batch flush for any queue once the oldest request reaches the configured limit (configurable via runtime config).
- Implements fairness-aware weight normalization across tenant queues so one tenant cannot monopolize GPU batches; weight decay keeps short bursts from permanently crowding out other queues.
- Adds a soft cap on batch width for high-throughput queues to leave slots for small important queues (prioritized via aging score).
- Small API: exposes new runtime flags batching.max_wait_ms, batching.age_priority_steps, batching.queue_weight_limits for tuning.
- Unit/integration tests and a perf benchmark harness to validate fairness and throughput trade-offs.

Design notes:
- The aging score is computed as a linear ramp that upgrades queue priority in discrete steps (age_priority_steps) to avoid noisy frequent re-sorts.
- Max-wait flush is implemented in the queue manager; it is conservative and only triggers when the estimate of next batch completion exceeds the threshold.
- Weight normalization uses a moving average of tokens processed per tenant to adapt to shifting workloads.

Checklist:
- [x] design approved (ENG-2148)
- [x] unit tests added for queue aging and max-wait behavior
- [x] integration tests for multi-tenant fairness and starvation scenarios
- [x] perf benchmark results attached
- [x] docs updated (docs/perf/continuous-batching.md)

Testing/Results:
- Microbenchmarks show ~3% throughput drop at extreme configs but 40-90% reduction in 99th-percentile latency for starved queues in mixed workloads. See perf/bench/continuous-batching-report-2026-01-18.md for details.
- CI: initial run failed a test around batch flush timing; fixed race in queue_manager by batching the timer reset operations (see commit 3).

Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag runtime.flags.enable_scheduler_fairness. Start with internal Dedicated clusters for 48h, then opt-in customers, then global. Monitor token-level latency, batch utilization, and queue fairness metrics (new metrics added: batching.queue_age_seconds, batching.queue_weight, batching.max_wait_flush_count).

Notes: this PR touches hot paths in the scheduler; changes are intentionally conservative. Further tuning will be driven by telemetry after rollout.

diff_snippets:
--- a/runtime/batching/weight_normalizer.go
+++ b/runtime/batching/weight_normalizer.go
@@ -1,0 +1,48 @@
+package batching
+
+// moving average of tokens per tenant used to normalize weights
+type weightNormalizer struct {
+    mu sync.Mutex
+    avg map[string]float64
+}
+
+func (w *weightNormalizer) Update(tenant string, tokens float64) {
+    w.mu.Lock(); defer w.mu.Unlock()
+    prev := w.avg[tenant]
+    w.avg[tenant] = prev*0.9 + tokens*0.1
+}

--- a/docs/perf/continuous-batching.md
+++ b/docs/perf/continuous-batching.md

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Overall design LGTM. Can you add a small note on how aging interacts with prefix caching? We should avoid evicting KV cache too aggressively when flushing partial batches.
Asha Patel: Good point — added comment and ensured flush does not evict prefix entries; flush only schedules currently-cached KV. See queue_manager.go commit.
Liam O'Connor: There's a potential race on timer reset; CI flagged a flake. I recommend consolidating timer reset under the same lock (see inline).
Asha Patel: Fixed in commit d2f9b5a; timer reset now under qm.mu and added deterministic test exercising the race.
Priya Rao: Tests look solid. Did you run the perf harness across Dedicated nodes? Curious about impact on batch utilization metrics.
Asha Patel: Yes — added perf report. Utilization drops ~3% in microbench for worst-case fairness configs; 99p latency improved significantly for small tenants.
notes: Rollout: internal -> opt-in -> global with telemetry gates
release_notes: Tuned continuous-batching scheduler: improves fairness and prevents starvation by introducing queue aging, max-wait flushes, and tenant weight normalization. Config flags: batching.max_wait_ms, batching.age_priority_steps, batching.queue_weight_limits. Release behind feature flag.
changelog: Implemented scheduler fairness heuristics and max-wait flush to reduce starvation; added unit/integration tests and perf report.
